title: Automatic Transmission External Controls
introduction: The selector lever, its cable and the steering-wheel paddles give the driver ways to interact with the automatic transmission. I follow the cable as the physical handshake between the cabin selector and the transmission, then keep the locking functions and paddle controls distinct. This overview identifies those parts and relationships; it does not provide cable adjustment, interlock testing or an emergency-release procedure.

edits.text: Selector Linkage, Locks and Paddle Controls
The transmission selector lever linkage includes these components:
edits.why: Start with the connection between the cabin selector and the transmission, then identify the actuator incorporated into the selector assembly.

edits.text: A selector lever cable connects the selector lever assembly to the transmission manual control lever.
edits.why: The cable provides the physical link between these assemblies. The transmission's manual control lever is the component named here, even though this article concerns an automatic transmission.

edits.text: A brake shift interlock actuator is integrated into the selector lever assembly.
edits.why: This locates the actuator within the selector assembly. Its operating logic and serviceability are not detailed in this overview.

edits.text: The workshop describes the following selector and ignition-lock relationships.
edits.why: I separate the mechanical interlock description from the labels on the actual controls: this Mustang uses keyless pushbutton ignition, while this workshop overview uses generic LOCK terminology.

edits.text: The workshop states that the selector assembly locks the transmission selector in P when the ignition is in LOCK.
edits.why: That is the source’s generic description of the parked interlock state, not an instruction to turn a physical key. The matching owner’s manual describes Off, On and Start modes using the pushbutton.

edits.text: The workshop states that the selector must be in P before the ignition can be turned to LOCK.
edits.why: For this pushbutton-equipped Mustang, the owner’s normal stationary-stop sequence uses PARK, the start/stop button and the parking brake. Use Starting and Stopping the Engine in the matching owner’s manual for the actual controls; there is no ignition lock cylinder requiring a physical key to be turned or removed.

edits.text: The steering wheel provides another transmission control:
Steering-wheel-mounted SelectShift™ paddle switches let the driver manually shift the transmission.
edits.why: The paddles provide driver shift requests from the steering wheel. Their detailed operating conditions are outside this overview.

editorialRevision.scope: Generic LOCK terminology attributed; actual pushbutton owner controls distinguished. Cable, interlock hardware and SelectShift behavior unchanged; full prior review preserved.
